newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent up on lower than expected Nov programme.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent up on lower than expected Nov programme.

text.p: IPE Brent futures strengthened on Wednesday after November's U.K. North Sea Brent crude loading programme turned out to be lower than expected, traders said.
November Brent, which expires at the close of Wednesday's session, was trading 24 cents up at $24.97 a barrel at 1021 GMT. December stood 27 cents higher at $24.38.
"The strength lies in the Brent cargoes programme. We were expecting 47 cargoes -- 42 have been announced," one trader said.
The programme will consist of 38 full 500,000-barrel cargoes and 2.17 million barrels in top-ups, crude traders said.
The Brent volumes scheduled to load in November were 2.26 million barrels less than the original October programme of 44 full cargoes and an additional 1.43 million barrels in top-ups.
Traders said $25 a barrel would be a critical point for the front month. "If it breaks that point in good volume, that would give further impetus," said a broker.
Traders said the November expiry could provoke a fair amount of activity.
"Anything can happen at expiry. People will probably start rolling November positions into December, but not until later on," one trader said.
